html:
Brasília is the capital of Brazil, a city planned from scratch and built in about four years on an empty plateau in the interior. It was opened in April 1960.

Moving the capital inland, away from Rio de Janeiro on the coast, had been an idea since the 1800s and was written into the constitution of 1891. President Juscelino Kubitschek made it happen, as the centrepiece of his promise of "fifty years of progress in five". The aim was to pull people and money into the empty middle of the country.

Lúcio Costa drew the city plan, shaped like an aeroplane or a bird, with government buildings along the central axis and housing blocks along the wings. Oscar Niemeyer designed the main buildings, among them the twin towers and bowls of the National Congress and the crown shaped cathedral. Roberto Burle Marx did much of the landscaping.

It became the most complete example of modernist city planning anywhere and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987. Critics say it was made for cars rather than people, and most workers ended up in satellite towns outside the plan.
sum: Brasília is the capital of Brazil, a city planned from scratch and built in about four years on an empty plateau in the interior. It was opened in April 1960.
